newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut BLC bank issues 1997 Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Beirut BLC bank issues 1997 Q1 results.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce reported on Monday unaudited consolidated pre-tax profits of 8.04 billion Lebanese pounds ($5.2 million) for the first quarter of 1997.

The bank said profits included 2.80 billion pounds ($1.81 million) realised on the sale of real estate assets. Interest expense during the same period represented 64.5 percent of interest income, down from 73 percent at the end of 1996.
Consolidated customer deposits rose 6.1 percent to 911.48 billion pounds ($589.67 million) from 858.95 billion pounds ($553.45 million) at the end of 1996.
Consolidated loans rose 2.6 percent to 336.99 billion pounds ($218 million) from 328.54 billion pounds ($211.69 million), the bank added in a statement.

Last December, BLC completed a $60 million capital increase through simultaneous local and international share offerings. The increase covered the acquisition of BLC France, its Paris subsidiary which split off during the 1975-1990 civil war.
BLC shares which started trading at 11.25 on December 30, traded at $17 on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Monday.
